edit.description: the foundations read ahead of the gate switch, and the doc that argues a fork is not handed down
the pickability cases over a forest whose goal declares the fork

summary: a `dependsOnForks` slug declared on an ancestor holds the entry, the way the ancestor's gate already does
acceptance: the foundations read folds the entry's ancestry as well as its own declaration, so a fork declared once on a goal holds its whole subtree whatever each descendant's gate says, and the doc that calls a fork "not what an ancestor hands down" goes with it
tests: an unresolved fork declared on an ancestor holds an entry whose own gate is open
the fork resolver is asked for every slug the entry's ancestry declares
pins: an entry none of whose ancestry declares a fork never invokes the resolver
notes: Measured on this tip: `isPickableNow` folds `gateSettled` over the entry and `ancestorsOf`, but reads `entry.dependsOnForks` alone, and its doc states the old ruling outright. Selection reaches the same read through `gateEligible`, so one fold answers both consumers.
